exposure: Group A: Spent more than 50% of labor in a recumbent position
Group B: Spent more than 50% of labor in alternative positions
cohort: 225 primiparous women with physiological pregnancies and single cephalic fetuses at term
finding: Alternative maternal positioning during labor may positively influence labor process, reducing maternal pain, operative vaginal delivery, cesarean section, and episiotomy rate.
mod_finding: Alternative maternal positioning during labor may positively influence the labor process, reducing maternal pain, operative vaginal delivery, cesarean section, and episiotomy rates.
